question: A particle has zero kinetic energy. What can be concluded about the particle's motion?
option_1: It is moving with high acceleration
option_4: It is moving with uniform velocity
solution_text:
The correct answer is It must be at rest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kinetic energy is given by KE = ½mv², where m is mass and v is velocity. (गतिज ऊर्जा — वस्तु की गति के कारण ऊर्जा)

 

• Since mass (m) of a particle is never zero, KE = 0 forces v = 0, i.e. the particle is not moving at all — it must be at rest.

 

• Momentum (p = mv) also becomes zero when v = 0, so momentum is minimum (zero), not maximum, ruling out Option C.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kinetic energy is always non-negative — it can be zero (at rest) or positive (in motion), but never negative.

 

• KE depends on the square of velocity, so doubling the speed makes KE four times as large.

 

• The work-energy theorem states that the work done by the net force on a body equals its change in kinetic energy.

 

NOTE

 

• High acceleration (Option A): A body can have zero velocity for an instant while still accelerating (e.g. a ball thrown up at its highest point), but 'zero KE' as a persistent statement about motion simply means v = 0.

 

• Maximum momentum (Option C): Momentum is directly proportional to velocity, so it is zero, not maximum, when KE is zero.

 

• Uniform velocity (Option D): Uniform velocity means constant non-zero speed, which would give non-zero KE.

question: From the given alternatives, which method of asexual reproduction involves the formation of a new plant from the broken portion of the parent plant?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fragmentation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fragmentation is a method of asexual reproduction in which the parent body (or plant) breaks into two or more pieces (fragments), and each fragment grows into a new complete individual. (खंडन — टूटे हुए भाग से नया पौधा)

 

• It is common in simple, filamentous organisms such as Spirogyra (a green alga) and in plants that can regenerate from stem or root cuttings, such as money plant, rose and sugarcane.

 

• Being asexual, fragmentation produces offspring that are genetically identical (clones) to the parent, since it does not involve fusion of gametes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other modes of asexual reproduction: binary fission (Amoeba, bacteria), budding (Hydra, yeast), spore formation (Rhizopus, ferns, mosses), and vegetative propagation (potato eyes, ginger rhizome).

 

• Regeneration, seen in organisms like Planaria and Hydra, is the ability to regrow lost body parts and is closely related to fragmentation.

 

• Asexual reproduction is generally faster and requires only a single parent, unlike sexual reproduction which needs two parents and produces genetic variation.

 

NOTE

 

• Fertilisation (Option A): The fusion of a male and a female gamete; this is a step in sexual, not asexual, reproduction.

 

• Binary fission (Option B): A single-celled organism divides into two equal, genetically identical daughter cells, e.g. Amoeba and bacteria.

 

• Spore formation (Option D): Tiny reproductive units called spores, produced inside a sporangium, are released and germinate into new individuals under favourable conditions, as in Rhizopus (bread mould).

question: Which statement best describes a homologous series of organic compounds?
option_1: A series of compounds having the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and consecutive members differing by a −CH2− group
option_2: A series of compounds that all have branched chains
option_3: A series of compounds with different functional groups but the same molecular formula
option_4: A series of elements with similar physical properties
solution_text:
The correct answer is A series of compounds having the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and consecutive members differing by a −CH2− group.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A homologous series is a family of organic compounds having the same functional group and the same general formula, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a −CH2− unit (14 u in molecular mass). (समजातीय श्रेणी — समान सामान्य सूत्र, CH2 का अंतर)

 

• Because they share the same functional group, all members of a homologous series show similar chemical properties, while their physical properties (like melting point, boiling point and density) show a gradual, steady change as molecular mass increases.

 

• Example: the alkane series (CH4, C2H6, C3H8, C4H10, ...) has the general formula CnH2n+2; the alcohol series (CH3OH, C2H5OH, ...) has the general formula CnH2n+1OH.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• General formulas of common homologous series: alkanes — CnH2n+2, alkenes — CnH2n, alkynes — CnH2n−2.

 

• All members of a homologous series can be prepared by similar general methods, which is why studying one member helps predict the behaviour of the whole series.

 

• A functional group is a specific atom or group of atoms (like −OH, −COOH, −CHO) that is mainly responsible for the characteristic chemical reactions of a compound.

 

NOTE

 

• Branched chains (Option B): Branching is a structural feature of some carbon compounds and is unrelated to the defining idea of a homologous series.

 

• Same molecular formula, different functional groups (Option C): This actually describes functional isomers, not a homologous series.

 

• Elements with similar physical properties (Option D): This is closer to the idea of groups in the periodic table (like alkali metals), not a homologous series of organic compounds.

question: Where is the centre of curvature of a convex mirror located?
option_2: At the pole of the mirror
option_3: At the principal focus of the mirror
solution_text:
The correct answer is Behind the mirror.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a convex mirror, the reflecting surface bulges outward (towards the object), so both the centre of curvature (C) and the principal focus (F) lie behind the mirror, on the side away from the object. (उत्तल दर्पण — वक्रता केंद्र दर्पण के पीछे)

 

• This is why a convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image located behind the mirror, between the pole and the focus, no matter where the object is placed.

 

• The radius of curvature (R) is the distance from the pole to the centre of curvature, and it is related to the focal length by f = R/2, a relation that holds for both concave and convex mirrors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a concave mirror, by contrast, the centre of curvature and focus lie in front of the mirror (on the same side as the object), which is why a concave mirror can form both real and virtual images.

 

• Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles and security mirrors in shops, because they give an erect image with a wider field of view.

 

• The pole (P) is the centre point of the mirror's reflecting surface, and the straight line through P and C is called the principal axis.

 

NOTE

 

• In front of the mirror (Option A): This is where the centre of curvature of a concave mirror lies, not a convex mirror.

 

• At the pole (Option B): The pole is a separate reference point on the mirror itself, not the same as the centre of curvature.

 

• At the principal focus (Option C): The focus (F) is the midpoint between the pole and the centre of curvature, not the centre of curvature itself.

question: A student connects a voltmeter across the terminals of a glowing bulb. What does the voltmeter measure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Potential difference across the bulb.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A voltmeter measures the potential difference (voltage) between two points of a circuit, and it is always connected in parallel across the component being measured. (वोल्टमीटर — विभवांतर मापने का यंत्र, समांतर क्रम में)

 

• An ideal voltmeter has a very high resistance, so that it draws negligible current from the circuit and does not disturb the reading.

 

• Since it is connected across the bulb's terminals, it directly measures the work done per unit charge in driving current through the bulb, i.e. the voltage across it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• An ammeter, in contrast, measures current and is connected in series in the circuit; an ideal ammeter has zero (very low) resistance.

 

• Ohm's Law relates the three quantities: V = IR, where V is potential difference, I is current, and R is resistance.

 

• The SI unit of potential difference is the volt (V), defined as 1 joule of work done per coulomb of charge (1 V = 1 J/C).

 

NOTE

 

• Heat produced (Option B): This is measured indirectly using Joule's law of heating, H = I²Rt; it is not what a voltmeter reads.

 

• Resistance (Option C): Resistance can be calculated from V and I readings (R = V/I) but is measured directly by an instrument called an ohmmeter, not a voltmeter alone.

 

• Current (Option D): Current is measured by an ammeter, which is connected in series, unlike the voltmeter.

question: A farmer lives near a river, but the canal system in his area receives an irregular water supply from the reservoir. What should he ideally adopt for irrigation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is River lift system.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a river lift system, water is directly lifted from the river using pumps, without depending on dams, canals or reservoirs, making it ideal when canal supply is irregular but a river is nearby. (नदी उत्थापन सिंचाई प्रणाली)

 

• Since the farmer lives near a river, tapping this dependable, direct source is more reliable than relying on the canal network, which in turn depends on reservoir releases and can suffer irregular supply.

 

• River lift irrigation is commonly used in areas where the land level is higher than the river, so water needs to be pumped up before it can flow into the fields by gravity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major traditional sources/methods of irrigation in India: canals, wells and tube wells, tanks, and river lift systems.

 

• Canal irrigation is the most widely used method in India, prominent in the northern plains (Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh) because of the flat terrain and perennial rivers.

 

• Modern micro-irrigation methods like drip and sprinkler irrigation are water-efficient and are promoted under schemes like Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY).

 

NOTE

 

• Flood irrigation (Option A): Water is allowed to flow freely over the field; it is water-wasteful and not a solution to an irregular source problem.

 

• Sprinklers only (Option C): Sprinklers are efficient for distributing water over the field but still require a dependable source of water to draw from, which is exactly the problem here.

 

• Wells (Option D): Wells tap groundwater and are useful, but a farmer living beside a perennial river has a more direct and often more dependable option in a river lift system.

question: What type of epithelial tissue is the outer skin made of?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stratified squamous epithelium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The outer skin (epidermis) is made of stratified squamous epithelium, consisting of many layers of flat, scale-like cells, which provides strong mechanical protection against wear and tear. (स्तरित शल्की उपकला — त्वचा)

 

• Being multi-layered, this tissue can withstand friction and continuously replaces its outermost dead cells as they wear off, protecting the softer tissues underneath.

 

• It also lines other body parts that are prone to abrasion, such as the inner lining of the mouth, oesophagus and vagina.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines cavities; its cells are tightly packed with little intercellular space, and it rests on a basement membrane.

 

• Types of epithelium are classified by cell shape (squamous, cuboidal, columnar) and number of layers (simple = single layer, stratified = many layers, e.g. skin, or ciliated columnar in the respiratory tract).

 

• Glandular epithelium is a modified form that is specialised for secretion, forming glands such as the salivary and sweat glands.

 

NOTE

 

• Columnar epithelium (Option B): Tall, pillar-shaped cells found in the lining of the intestine, suited for absorption and secretion.

 

• Cuboidal epithelium (Option C): Cube-shaped cells found in kidney tubules and salivary gland ducts, involved in secretion and absorption.

 

• Simple squamous epithelium (Option D): A single layer of flat cells found in the lining of blood vessels and alveoli, suited for diffusion/filtration, but too fragile to serve as the body's outer protective layer.

question: The formula unit mass of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a formula unit of a/an:
solution_text:
The correct answer is compound.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The formula unit mass is the term used for ionic compounds, and it is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms present in one formula unit of that compound. (सूत्र इकाई द्रव्यमान — आयनिक यौगिक)

 

• It is used for ionic compounds like NaCl (which do not exist as discrete molecules but as a giant lattice of ions), whereas the term molecular mass is used for covalent, molecule-forming compounds like water or carbon dioxide.

 

• Example: the formula unit mass of NaCl = atomic mass of Na (23 u) + atomic mass of Cl (35.5 u) = 58.5 u.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Atomic mass is the mass of a single atom of an element expressed in atomic mass units (u), based on the carbon-12 scale.

 

• Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule, e.g. the molecular mass of water (H2O) = 2(1) + 16 = 18 u.

 

• Mole concept: one mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number) and has a mass equal to its molar mass expressed in grams.

 

NOTE

 

• Atom (Option A): A single atom has only an atomic mass; the concept of a 'formula unit' applies to a combination of atoms/ions, not a lone atom.

 

• Mixture (Option C): A mixture does not have a fixed formula or fixed composition, so the term formula unit mass does not apply to it.

 

• Element (Option D): For elements that exist as molecules (like O2), the term used is molecular mass, calculated from atomic mass, not 'formula unit mass'.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the nucleus?
option_2: Nuclear membrane is a double-layered structure.
option_3: Nuclear membrane is a non-porous and rigid structure.
option_4: Nucleus plays a central role in cellular reproduction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nuclear membrane is a non-porous and rigid structure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The nuclear membrane (nuclear envelope) is a double-layered structure, but it is not non-porous — it is studded with tiny nuclear pores that allow the exchange of RNA and proteins between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, so this statement is incorrect. (केंद्रक झिल्ली — छिद्रयुक्त, दोहरी परत)

 

• The nucleus contains chromatin material, which condenses into chromosomes during cell division; chromosomes carry the genetic information in the form of DNA.

 

• The nucleus controls and directs cellular reproduction and heredity, since it houses the DNA that governs protein synthesis and the transmission of genetic traits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nucleus is often called the 'control centre' or 'brain' of the cell because it regulates all major cellular activities.

 

• Inside the nucleus, the nucleolus is a dense, non-membranous region responsible for ribosome synthesis.

 

• Robert Brown discovered the nucleus in 1831 while examining orchid cells under a microscope.

 

NOTE

 

• Nucleus contains chromosomes (Option A): This is a correct statement — chromosomes, made of DNA and protein, are found inside the nucleus.

 

• Nuclear membrane is double-layered (Option B): This is also correct — it consists of an outer and an inner membrane with a perinuclear space between them.

 

• Central role in cellular reproduction (Option D): Correct, since the nucleus controls DNA replication and cell division through mitosis and meiosis.

question: A particle's velocity-time graph is a straight line with a negative slope. What does this indicate about the particle's motion?
option_2: The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.
option_3: The particle is moving with increasing acceleration.
option_4: The particle is speeding up in the positive direction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On a velocity-time (v-t) graph, the slope represents acceleration. A straight line with negative slope means the particle has a constant negative acceleration (retardation). (वेग-समय ग्राफ का ऋणात्मक ढाल — मंदन)

 

• If the particle is moving in the positive direction (v > 0) while acceleration is negative, the velocity keeps decreasing in magnitude — that is, the particle is slowing down.

 

• Since it is a straight line, the acceleration is uniform (constant), not increasing, which rules out any option describing 'increasing' acceleration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A horizontal line (zero slope) on a v-t graph means constant velocity (zero acceleration).

 

• The area under a v-t graph gives the displacement of the particle over that time interval.

 

• On a position-time graph, the slope gives velocity, whereas on a velocity-time graph, the slope gives acceleration — a common point of confusion in exams.

 

NOTE

 

• At rest (Option A): A particle at rest would show a horizontal line at v = 0 on the graph, not a sloped line.

 

• Increasing acceleration (Option C): This would require a curved v-t graph (increasing slope), not a straight line, since a straight line means constant acceleration.

 

• Speeding up in positive direction (Option D): This would require velocity to increase with time, i.e. a positive slope, not a negative one.

question: The expression for acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet of mass M and radius R is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is g = GM/R².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The acceleration due to gravity at the surface of a planet is given by g = GM/R², where G is the universal gravitational constant, M is the mass of the planet, and R is its radius. (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण — g = GM/R²)

 

• This is derived by equating the gravitational force on a small mass m at the surface, F = GMm/R², with F = mg (Newton's second law), which on cancelling m gives g = GM/R².

 

• On Earth, this formula gives g ≈ 9.8 m/s², using G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², M ≈ 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg and R ≈ 6.4 × 10⁶ m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since g ∝ M/R², g is greater on more massive planets and smaller on planets with larger radius, for the same mass.

 

• The value of g decreases as one moves away from the Earth's surface (with altitude) and also as one goes towards the centre of the Earth (with depth), becoming zero at the centre.

 

• g is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator on Earth, because the Earth is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator.

 

NOTE

 

• g = GR/M² (Option A): Incorrectly places R in the numerator and M² in the denominator; this does not match the correct dependence of g on mass and radius.

 

• g = GM²/R (Option C): Incorrectly uses M² instead of M, and R instead of R².

 

• g = R/GM² (Option D): Places G in the denominator, which is dimensionally and physically inconsistent with the correct law of gravitation.

question: Which of the following reactions demonstrates the acidic nature of ethanoic acid?
option_2: Ethanoic acid + Sodium → Sodium ethanoate + Hydrogen gas
option_3: Ethanoic acid + Methanol → Methanoic acid + Ethane
option_4: Ethanoic acid + Sodium hydroxide → Sodium ethanoate + Water
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanoic acid + Sodium hydroxide → Sodium ethanoate + Water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reaction of ethanoic acid with a base (sodium hydroxide) to form a salt (sodium ethanoate) and water is a classic acid-base neutralisation reaction, the most direct demonstration of the acidic character of ethanoic acid. (एथेनोइक अम्ल का उदासीनीकरण)

 

• CH3COOH + NaOH → CH3COONa + H2O — here ethanoic acid donates a proton to the hydroxide ion, exactly the defining behaviour of an acid reacting with a base.

 

• Ethanoic acid (also called acetic acid) is a weak carboxylic acid, present in vinegar (5-8% acetic acid in water), and turns blue litmus red.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethanoic acid also reacts with carbonates and bicarbonates to liberate carbon dioxide, e.g. with sodium carbonate: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2, which is another standard test for an acid.

 

• Ethanoic acid has the molecular formula CH3COOH and contains the −COOH (carboxyl) functional group, characteristic of all carboxylic acids.

 

• Reaction with ethanol (Option A) in the presence of a catalyst produces a sweet-smelling ester (ethyl ethanoate), called esterification — this demonstrates the reactivity of the −COOH group but is not the acid-base test.

 

NOTE

 

• Ethanoic acid + Ethanol (Option A): This is esterification, producing an ester and water; it shows the reactivity of the carboxyl group, not the acidic (proton-donating) nature towards a base.

 

• Ethanoic acid + Sodium (Option B): This reaction with an active metal does release hydrogen gas (a general property of acids reacting with reactive metals), but the standard textbook reaction chosen to demonstrate acidity is the neutralisation with a base.

 

• Ethanoic acid + Methanol (Option C): This equation as written is chemically incorrect — reacting with methanol under esterification conditions would give methyl ethanoate and water, not methanoic acid and ethane.

question: What are the main components of a neuron?
option_1: Dendrites, cell body, axon and nerve endings
option_3: Cell body, dendrites, nerve endings and synapse
option_4: Dendrites, cell body and nerve endings
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dendrites, cell body and axon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A neuron (nerve cell) is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system, and its main components are the dendrites, cell body (cyton) and axon. (न्यूरॉन — द्रुमिका, कोशिका काय, तंत्रिकाक्ष)

 

• Dendrites are branched extensions that receive signals from other neurons; the cell body (containing the nucleus) processes the signal; the axon, often covered by a fatty myelin sheath, carries the nerve impulse away from the cell body towards another neuron or an effector organ.

 

• At the tip of the axon are nerve endings (axon terminals), which release chemical messengers called neurotransmitters at a junction called the synapse to pass the impulse to the next neuron.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The pathway of an electrical impulse in a neuron: dendrite → cell body → axon → axon terminal (nerve ending) → synapse.

 

• Neurons are classified as sensory neurons (carry impulses from receptors to the CNS), motor neurons (carry impulses from the CNS to effectors), and relay/interneurons (connect sensory and motor neurons within the CNS).

 

• A group of neuron fibres bound together forms a nerve; nerves and the brain and spinal cord together make up the nervous system.

 

NOTE

 

• With nerve endings added (Option A): Nerve endings are a part of the axon's terminal structure, an additional detail, but the three fundamental, defining components taught at this level are dendrite, cell body and axon.

 

• Cell body, dendrites, nerve endings and synapse (Option C): This list omits the axon — the actual conducting fibre of the neuron — which is essential.

 

• Dendrites, cell body and nerve endings (Option D): This list also omits the axon, replacing it with just the nerve endings, which are only the terminal part of the axon.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT true according to the sign convention for spherical lenses?
option_1: The focal length of a concave lens is negative.
option_2: Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.
option_3: The focal length of a convex lens is positive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the New Cartesian sign convention for spherical lenses, all distances are measured from the optical centre, and heights measured upwards (above the principal axis) are taken as positive, while heights measured downwards are negative — so the given statement is NOT true. (नई कार्तीय चिह्न परिपाटी — ऊपर की ऊँचाई धनात्मक)

 

• Since objects are conventionally placed above the principal axis with an upward (positive) height, the object height is always positive, never negative, in the standard convention.

 

• Under this same convention: object distance is always negative (as the object is placed to the left, against the direction of incident light), the focal length of a convex lens is positive, and the focal length of a concave lens is negative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sign convention rules at a glance: all distances measured from the optical centre; distances in the direction of incident light are positive, against it are negative; heights above the axis are positive, below are negative.

 

• The lens formula is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f, and magnification m = h'/h = v/u, both of which depend on this sign convention for correct interpretation of results.

 

• A positive magnification indicates an erect (virtual) image, while a negative magnification indicates an inverted (real) image.

 

NOTE

 

• Concave lens focal length negative (Option A): This is a correct statement under the convention, since concave lenses diverge light and their focus lies on the same side as the object.

 

• Convex lens focal length positive (Option C): Correct — convex lenses converge light to a real focus on the far side, giving a positive focal length.

 

• Object distance negative (Option D): Correct — since the object is always placed on the left of the lens (against the direction of light), its distance is taken as negative.

question: The distributions of electrons in the K, L, and M shell of the chlorine atom are:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2, 8, 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorine (Cl) has atomic number 17, meaning a neutral atom has 17 electrons, distributed in shells as K = 2, L = 8, M = 7, following the Bohr-Bury scheme. (क्लोरीन — इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास 2, 8, 7)

 

• Electrons fill shells using the 2n² rule (maximum electrons in the nth shell = 2n²): K-shell (n=1) holds up to 2, L-shell (n=2) holds up to 8, M-shell (n=3) holds up to 18 (but only 7 remain to be placed here for chlorine, since 2+8=10 electrons are already used, leaving 17−10 = 7).

 

• With 7 electrons in its outermost (valence) shell, chlorine needs just 1 more electron to complete its octet, which explains its strong tendency to gain one electron and form a −1 (Cl⁻) ion, making it highly reactive.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorine belongs to Group 17 (the halogens) and Period 3 of the periodic table.

 

• The valency of chlorine is 1, since it needs one electron to attain a stable noble-gas-like configuration (argon's configuration, 2, 8, 8).

 

• Elements with a similar valence-shell pattern: Fluorine (Z=9): 2, 7; Bromine (Z=35): 2, 8, 18, 7 — all halogens have 7 electrons in their outermost shell.

 

NOTE

 

• 2, 7, 7 (Option A): Incorrect — this violates the 2n² rule, since the L-shell can hold up to 8 electrons and would be filled before the M-shell gets any.

 

• 2, 6, 5 (Option B) and 2, 7, 8 (Option D): Both add up to only 13 or leave the shells improperly filled; they do not correctly represent chlorine's 17 electrons distributed shell-by-shell in order (K first, then L, then M).

question: What is the type of reproduction beginning from the fusion of male and female gametes called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sexual reproduction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sexual reproduction is the process in which a male gamete (sperm) fuses with a female gamete (egg/ovum) in a process called fertilisation, forming a zygote that develops into a new individual. (लैंगिक जनन — युग्मकों का संलयन)

 

• Because it combines genetic material from two parents, sexual reproduction produces offspring with genetic variation, which is important for a species' ability to adapt and survive changing environments.

 

• The gametes themselves are produced by a special type of cell division called meiosis, which halves the chromosome number so that fertilisation restores the normal (diploid) chromosome number in the zygote.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fertilisation can be external (as in most fish and frogs, where fusion occurs outside the body) or internal (as in humans and most terrestrial animals, occurring inside the female body).

 

• In flowering plants, sexual reproduction involves pollination (transfer of pollen from anther to stigma) followed by fertilisation, leading to the formation of a seed and eventually a fruit.

 

• Sexual reproduction is generally slower than asexual reproduction and requires two parents, unlike asexual methods which need only one.

 

NOTE

 

• Budding (Option B): An asexual method in which a small outgrowth (bud) develops on the parent body and eventually detaches as a new organism, seen in Hydra and yeast.

 

• Cloning (Option C): A technique/process that produces a genetically identical copy of an organism without the fusion of gametes; it is an asexual/artificial method, not natural sexual reproduction.

 

• Binary fission (Option D): A single parent cell simply splits into two equal daughter cells, as seen in Amoeba and bacteria; no gametes are involved.

question: According to Newton's second law of motion, what happens when an unbalanced force is applied to an object?
option_2: The object moves in a circular path
option_3: The object's momentum changes in the direction of the applied force
option_4: The object comes to rest immediately
solution_text:
The correct answer is The object's momentum changes in the direction of the applied force.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's second law of motion states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the applied unbalanced force, and this change takes place in the direction of the force. (न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम — बल = संवेग परिवर्तन की दर)

 

• Mathematically, F = ma = m(v−u)/t, which comes from the more general statement F = Δp/Δt (force equals rate of change of momentum p = mv).

 

• Since momentum p = mv, and the applied unbalanced force changes the object's velocity (accelerates or decelerates it, or changes its direction), the momentum necessarily changes in the direction of the applied force, whether the object was initially at rest or moving.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's first law (law of inertia) states that an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced (net) force — this is the special case where F = 0, so momentum stays constant.

 

• Newton's third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), defined as the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a mass of 1 kg (1 N = 1 kg m/s²).

 

NOTE

 

• Momentum remains unchanged (Option A): This would be true only if the net force were zero (balanced forces), which contradicts the question's premise of an unbalanced force.

 

• Moves in a circular path (Option B): Circular motion requires a specific type of unbalanced force, i.e. a centripetal force acting perpendicular to velocity at every instant; it is not a general consequence of any unbalanced force.

 

• Comes to rest immediately (Option D): An unbalanced force changes the state of motion, but it does not necessarily bring the object to rest — it could speed it up, slow it down or change its direction, depending on the force's direction.

question: Two wires, A and B, of the same material, have the same length, but the cross-sectional area of wire A is twice that of wire B. The ratio of their resistances RA : RB is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 : 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The resistance of a wire is given by R = ρL/A, where ρ is the resistivity (a material property), L is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area, so resistance is inversely proportional to area (R ∝ 1/A) for wires of the same material and length. (प्रतिरोध — R = ρL/A)

 

• Since both wires are of the same material (same ρ) and same length (L), only the area varies, and area of A is twice that of B, i.e. A_A = 2A_B.

 

• R_A/R_B = A_B/A_A = A_B/(2A_B) = 1/2, so R_A : R_B = 1 : 2 — the thicker wire (A) has less resistance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Resistivity (ρ) depends only on the material and temperature of the conductor, not on its length or area — this is what distinguishes it from resistance.

 

• Good conductors like silver and copper have very low resistivity, which is why copper is the standard material for electrical wiring.

 

• For resistors in series, the equivalent resistance is the sum (R = R1+R2+...); for resistors in parallel, it is given by 1/R = 1/R1+1/R2+..., which is always less than the smallest individual resistance.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 : 1 (Option A): This would be the ratio if resistance were directly (not inversely) proportional to area — a common mistake.

 

• 1 : 1 (Option B): This would only be correct if the areas (or another compensating factor) were equal, which is not the case here.

 

• 4 : 1 (Option D): This would arise only if resistance depended on the square of the area ratio, which is not how the R = ρL/A formula works.

question: Which of the following is a molecule of a compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is H2O.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A molecule of a compound is formed when atoms of two or more different elements chemically combine in a fixed ratio; H2O (water) is made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms, two different elements, so it is a molecular compound. (यौगिक का अणु — भिन्न-भिन्न तत्वों का संयोजन)

 

• In contrast, a molecule of an element is formed when atoms of the same element combine, such as N2 (two nitrogen atoms), O2 (two oxygen atoms) and H2 (two hydrogen atoms) — all of which involve only one type of element.

 

• Water's chemical formula, H2O, shows 2 atoms of hydrogen combined with 1 atom of oxygen in a fixed ratio, which is characteristic of all compounds (they always have a fixed composition by mass).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Compounds have properties entirely different from their constituent elements — e.g. hydrogen and oxygen are both gases that support combustion, but water is a liquid that extinguishes fire.

 

• Compounds can be broken down into simpler substances only by chemical means (like electrolysis), unlike mixtures which can be separated by physical means.

 

• Other common examples of molecules of compounds: CO2 (carbon dioxide), NaCl (sodium chloride), NH3 (ammonia), CH4 (methane).

 

NOTE

 

• N2 (Option A): A diatomic molecule of the element nitrogen — both atoms are of the same type, so it is a molecule of an element, not a compound.

 

• O2 (Option C): A diatomic molecule of the element oxygen, again just one type of atom, making it a molecule of an element.

 

• H2 (Option D): A diatomic molecule of the element hydrogen; like N2 and O2, it consists of only one kind of atom.

question:
Select the correct statement from the following.

 

A) The large spaces between gas particles allow them to be easily squeezed into smaller volumes.

B) Gas particles have a high average kinetic energy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. According to the kinetic theory of matter, gas particles are far apart with large intermolecular spaces, which is exactly why gases can be compressed easily into smaller volumes. (गैस के कण — दूर-दूर, उच्च गतिज ऊर्जा)

 

• Gas particles also move randomly and rapidly in all directions, which gives them a high average kinetic energy compared to particles of solids and liquids at the same temperature.

 

• These two properties together explain the general characteristics of gases: they have no fixed shape or volume, exert pressure on the walls of their container due to constant collisions, and diffuse rapidly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The states of matter differ mainly in the arrangement, spacing and energy of their particles: solids have particles closely packed with least kinetic energy; liquids have particles moderately spaced; gases have particles most widely spaced with maximum kinetic energy.

 

• Diffusion (the spontaneous intermixing of particles of two substances) occurs fastest in gases, slower in liquids, and slowest in solids, directly reflecting the difference in kinetic energy and spacing.

 

• Boyle's law (at constant temperature, pressure and volume of a gas are inversely proportional) and Charles's law (at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature) are direct consequences of these particle properties.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither A nor B / Only B / Only A (Options A, B, D): Each of these under-counts the correct statements — both the given statements about gas particles (large spacing enabling compression, and high average kinetic energy) are standard, well-established facts of the kinetic theory.

question: The speed of sound (v) is calculated by multiplying which two wave properties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wavelength and Frequency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The speed of a wave (including sound) is given by the fundamental wave equation v = νλ (speed = frequency × wavelength), where ν (or f) is the frequency and λ is the wavelength. (ध्वनि की चाल = आवृत्ति × तरंगदैर्घ्य)

 

• Wavelength (λ) is the distance between two consecutive compressions (or rarefactions) of a sound wave, while frequency (ν) is the number of complete oscillations (or wavelengths) passing a point per second, measured in hertz (Hz).

 

• This relation shows that for a fixed speed (like sound in a given medium at a given temperature), wavelength and frequency are inversely proportional — a higher-pitched (higher-frequency) sound has a shorter wavelength.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The speed of sound in air at 22°C is about 344 m/s; it is greatest in solids, less in liquids, and least in gases, because sound needs a material medium and travels faster through more closely packed particles.

 

• Amplitude determines the loudness of a sound (larger amplitude = louder sound), not its speed.

 

• Time period (T) is the time taken for one complete oscillation and is the reciprocal of frequency (T = 1/ν).

 

NOTE

 

• Wavelength and Amplitude (Option B): Amplitude affects loudness, not speed, so multiplying it with wavelength does not give the correct speed relation.

 

• Amplitude and Time Period (Option C) and Amplitude and Frequency (Option D): Both incorrectly involve amplitude, which has no role in determining the speed of a wave; only wavelength and frequency (or equivalently, wavelength divided by time period) give the speed.

question: What happens if one drop of acid rain water is put on blue litmus paper?
option_1: Blue litmus paper will turn black.
option_2: No colour changes in litmus paper.
option_3: Blue litmus paper will turn yellow.
option_4: Blue litmus paper will turn red.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Blue litmus paper will turn red.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acid rain is rainwater made acidic (pH below 5.6) mainly due to dissolved oxides of sulphur and nitrogen released by burning fossil fuels, forming sulphuric acid and nitric acid. (अम्लीय वर्षा — नीले लिटमस को लाल करती है)

 

• Litmus is a natural indicator (obtained from lichens) that turns blue litmus paper red in the presence of an acid; since acid rain is acidic, it will turn blue litmus paper red.

 

• This is the standard laboratory test used to distinguish acids from bases: an acid turns blue litmus red, while a base turns red litmus blue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acid rain damages monuments made of marble (like the Taj Mahal, a phenomenon called 'marble cancer'), harms aquatic life by lowering the pH of water bodies, and damages crops and forests.

 

• Common natural indicators besides litmus: turmeric (turns red/pink in bases), china rose (Gudhal) extract, and red cabbage extract.

 

• Synthetic indicators like phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base) and methyl orange (red in acid, yellow in base) are also widely used in laboratories.

 

NOTE

 

• Turns black (Option A): Litmus paper does not turn black on contact with an acid; this is not a real indicator reaction.

 

• No colour change (Option B): Since acid rain is acidic, it will definitely react with and change the colour of blue litmus paper.

 

• Turns yellow (Option C): A yellow colour change is typical of indicators like methyl orange in a base, not of litmus reacting with an acid.

question: In human female, when egg is not fertilised, which of the following process takes place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Menstruation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• If the released egg is not fertilised, it survives for about one day, after which the thickened, blood-rich uterine lining (endometrium) built up to receive a fertilised egg is no longer needed and breaks down, being shed through the vagina as menstruation. (मासिक धर्म — अनिषेचित अंडे पर गर्भाशय की परत का बहना)

 

• Menstruation occurs roughly every 28 days as part of the menstrual cycle, and typically lasts about 3 to 5 days; it marks the absence of pregnancy in that cycle.

 

• If, instead, the egg is fertilised by a sperm, it forms a zygote, which implants in the uterine wall and develops into an embryo, and menstruation does not occur during that pregnancy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The menstrual cycle is regulated by hormones — mainly oestrogen and progesterone, along with the pituitary hormones FSH and LH, which also control ovulation (release of the egg from the ovary, typically around day 14).

 

• The first menstruation in a girl's life is called menarche, and the permanent stopping of menstrual cycles later in life is called menopause.

 

• Fertilisation normally occurs in the fallopian tube (oviduct), and the resulting embryo travels down to implant in the uterus.

 

NOTE

 

• Embryo development (Option A): This occurs only after successful fertilisation and implantation, i.e. when pregnancy has actually begun.

 

• Zygote formation (Option B): A zygote is formed only when the egg is fertilised by a sperm — the opposite of the situation described in the question.

 

• Parturition (Option C): This term refers to the process of childbirth at the end of a full pregnancy, not to what happens when fertilisation fails to occur.

question: Which of the following human activities contributes to ozone layer depletion?
option_2: Using CFC-based refrigerants and spray cans
solution_text:
The correct answer is Using CFC-based refrigerants and spray cans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), once widely used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol spray cans, rise into the stratosphere where UV radiation breaks them down, releasing chlorine atoms that destroy ozone (O3) molecules. (क्लोरोफ्लोरोकार्बन — ओजोन परत क्षरण)

 

• A single chlorine atom released from a CFC molecule can destroy thousands of ozone molecules in a chain reaction, making CFCs one of the most potent ozone-depleting substances.

 

• The depleted ozone layer (located in the stratosphere) normally absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV-B) radiation, so its thinning allows more UV rays to reach the Earth's surface, increasing risks like skin cancer and cataracts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Montreal Protocol (1987) is the international treaty that successfully led to a global phase-out of ozone-depleting substances, including CFCs.

 

• The 'ozone hole' is a region of severe ozone depletion observed mainly over Antarctica, especially pronounced during the southern spring (September-November).

 

• Other activities like conserving water, composting organic waste and using solar energy (Options A, C, D) are all environmentally friendly, sustainable practices that help reduce pollution, not cause it.

 

NOTE

 

• Conserving water (Option A): A positive, eco-friendly practice that reduces stress on freshwater resources, unrelated to ozone depletion.

 

• Composting organic waste (Option C): An environmentally beneficial practice that reduces landfill waste and produces useful manure; it does not release ozone-depleting substances.

 

• Using solar energy (Option D): A clean, renewable source of energy that helps reduce pollution and greenhouse gases, the opposite of an ozone-harming activity.

question: Which of the following products is formed when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide (lime water)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium carbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When carbon dioxide gas is passed through lime water [Ca(OH)2], it reacts to form a white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) and water: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 → CaCO3 + H2O. (चूने के पानी में CO2 — कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट का सफेद अवक्षेप)

 

• This reaction turns lime water milky, and it is the standard laboratory test used to detect the presence of carbon dioxide gas.

 

• If excess CO2 is passed further through this milky solution, the insoluble calcium carbonate reacts further to form soluble calcium bicarbonate [Ca(HCO3)2], and the milkiness disappears: CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 → Ca(HCO3)2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lime water is prepared by dissolving quicklime (calcium oxide, CaO) in water: CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime), which is itself formed by heating limestone (calcium carbonate).

 

• Calcium carbonate occurs naturally as limestone, marble and chalk, and is a key ingredient in cement manufacture and in the shells of many marine organisms.

 

• Similarly, passing CO2 into water forms carbonic acid (H2CO3), a weak acid, which is why carbonated drinks are mildly acidic and rainwater is naturally slightly acidic even without pollution.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcium oxide (Option B): This is quicklime, the starting material used to prepare lime water (calcium hydroxide); it is not the product of the reaction with CO2.

 

• Sodium carbonate (Option C): This compound contains sodium, an element not present anywhere in this reaction between calcium hydroxide and carbon dioxide.

 

• Calcium bicarbonate (Option D): This is formed only when excess CO2 is passed through the milky solution formed after the initial reaction, not from the first/direct reaction described.

question: A train of length 239 m takes 20 seconds to pass another train 161 m long coming from the opposite direction. If the speed of the first train is 43 km/hr, then find speed of the second train.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 29 km/hr.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train 1 length = 239 m, Train 2 length = 161 m, time to cross each other = 20 s (opposite directions), speed of Train 1 = 43 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance to be covered while crossing = sum of lengths = 239 + 161 = 400 m.

 

• Relative speed = distance ÷ time = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/hr.

 

• Since the trains move in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of individual speeds. So speed of Train 2 = 72 − 43 = 29 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert relative speed directly: (sum of lengths ÷ time) × 18/5 gives km/hr in one step; then subtract the known speed.

 

NOTE

 

• For opposite directions, relative speed = sum of speeds; for the same direction, relative speed = difference of speeds — mixing these up is the most common error.

question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 42.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 8 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5°.

 

GIVEN

 

• T is the intersection of the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S of quadrilateral PQRS; ∠STR = 42.5°; ∠P : ∠Q = 8 : 9.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard result: when the bisectors of two adjacent angles ∠R and ∠S of a quadrilateral meet at T, ∠STR = ½(∠P + ∠Q).

 

• So ∠P + ∠Q = 2 × 42.5° = 85°.

 

• Let ∠P = 8x and ∠Q = 9x. Then 8x + 9x = 85° ⇒ 17x = 85° ⇒ x = 5°.

 

• ∠P = 40°, ∠Q = 45°. Difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 45° − 40° = 5°.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Directly: difference = (9−8)x = x = 85°/17 = 5°, without separately computing ∠P and ∠Q.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorise the standard quadrilateral bisector result: the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles equals half the sum of the other two angles.

question: The average age of 43 students of a class is 13 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 14 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 57.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 43 students = 13 years; average age of 43 students + 1 teacher = 14 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of ages of 43 students = 43 × 13 = 559 years.

 

• Sum of ages of (43 students + teacher) = 44 × 14 = 616 years.

 

• Age of teacher = 616 − 559 = 57 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = old average + (number of students) × (increase in average) = 13 + 43 × 1 = 13 + 44 = 57. (The teacher's age exceeds the old average by the total increase distributed over all 44 people, i.e. by 44 × 1, added to the old average of 13.)

 

NOTE

 

• Sum = average × count; always convert to totals first when a new member changes the average — this avoids sign errors.

question: From the top of a building 15 m high, the angle of depression to a point on the ground is 45 degrees. Find the horizontal distance from the building to the point.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 15 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Height of building = 15 m; angle of depression from the top to a point on the ground = 45°.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the ground point to the top (alternate angles, since the horizontal line from the top is parallel to the ground).

 

• In the right triangle formed: tan(45°) = height ÷ horizontal distance = 15 ÷ d.

 

• Since tan(45°) = 1, we get 1 = 15 ÷ d ⇒ d = 15 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever the angle is exactly 45°, the horizontal distance always equals the height (since tan 45° = 1) — no calculation needed beyond reading off the height.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is printed in the source answer key as "B).5 m" — a formatting glitch in the original document; it does not affect the correct working, which clearly gives 15 m for a 45° angle of depression.

question: When x is added to each of 10, 14, 38 and 28, then the numbers so obtained, in this order, are in proportion. Then, if 3x : y :: y : (5x − 6), and y > 0, what is the value of y?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• (10+x), (14+x), (38+x), (28+x) are in proportion (in this order); also 3x : y :: y : (5x−6), y > 0.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Proportion means (10+x)/(14+x) = (38+x)/(28+x).

 

• Cross-multiplying: (10+x)(28+x) = (14+x)(38+x) ⇒ 280 + 38x + x² = 532 + 52x + x².

 

• 280 + 38x = 532 + 52x ⇒ −252 = 14x ⇒ x = −18.

 

• Now use 3x : y :: y : (5x−6), i.e. y² = 3x × (5x−6). Here 3x = −54 and 5x−6 = −90−6 = −96.

 

• y² = (−54) × (−96) = 5184 ⇒ y = √5184 = 72 (taking the positive root since y > 0).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In a proportion a:b::c:d, product of extremes = product of means; use this directly (y² = 3x(5x−6)) once x is found, and always take the positive square root when told y > 0.

 

NOTE

 

• A negative value of x is mathematically valid here since 'adding x' does not require x to be positive — do not discard it without checking the final constraint (y > 0), which is what actually decides the sign to keep.

question: The income of Raman is ₹43,800. He saves 20% of his income. If his income increases by 36% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. increase by ₹1,752.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income = ₹43,800; savings = 20% of income; new income = old income + 36%; new expenditure = old expenditure + 40%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Old expenditure = 80% of 43,800 = ₹35,040. Old savings = 43,800 − 35,040 = ₹8,760.

 

• New income = 43,800 × 1.36 = ₹59,568.

 

• New expenditure = 35,040 × 1.40 = ₹49,056.

 

• New savings = 59,568 − 49,056 = ₹10,512.

 

• Change in savings = 10,512 − 8,760 = increase of ₹1,752.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Work entirely with the increase amounts: increase in income = 0.36 × 43,800 = 15,768; increase in expenditure = 0.40 × 35,040 = 14,016; change in savings = 15,768 − 14,016 = 1,752 increase.

 

NOTE

 

• Always find the base expenditure first (income − savings) before applying its own percentage increase — applying 40% to the wrong base is the most common slip in this type of question.

question:
Simplify the following.

(a³ − b³)/(a² + ab + b²) + (a³ + b³)/(a² − ab + b²)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2a.

 

GIVEN

 

• (a³ − b³)/(a² + ab + b²) + (a³ + b³)/(a² − ab + b²).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the standard identities: a³ − b³ = (a−b)(a² + ab + b²) and a³ + b³ = (a+b)(a² − ab + b²).

 

• First term = (a−b)(a² + ab + b²)/(a² + ab + b²) = (a − b), after cancelling the common factor.

 

• Second term = (a+b)(a² − ab + b²)/(a² − ab + b²) = (a + b), after cancelling the common factor.

 

• Sum = (a − b) + (a + b) = 2a.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise a³±b³ factorisations on sight — the denominators are built exactly to cancel with these standard factors, so the whole expression collapses to (a−b)+(a+b) = 2a instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always keep a³ − b³ = (a−b)(a²+ab+b²) and a³ + b³ = (a+b)(a²−ab+b²) memorised — they appear repeatedly in simplification questions.

question: X people were given a contract for doing a piece of work in 36 days. 3 people did not turn up to work due to sickness, and the rest of the people completed the work in 39 days. What is the value of X?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 39.

 

GIVEN

 

• X people can finish the work in 36 days; (X−3) people actually took 39 days to finish it.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total work is constant, measured in man-days: X × 36 = (X − 3) × 39.

 

• 36X = 39X − 117 ⇒ −3X = −117 ⇒ X = 39.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up 'people × days = constant work' directly and solve the linear equation in one step — this is faster than trying to find individual work rates.

 

NOTE

 

• In work-and-time questions, (number of workers) × (number of days) = total work (in man-days) stays constant unless efficiency changes are mentioned.

question: A class of 75 students took a Physics test. 22 students had an average score of 85. The other students had an average score of 95. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 92.1.

 

GIVEN

 

• 75 students total; 22 students average 85; remaining (75−22) = 53 students average 95.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total marks of the 22 students = 22 × 85 = 1,870.

 

• Total marks of the remaining 53 students = 53 × 95 = 5,035.

 

• Total marks of the whole class = 1,870 + 5,035 = 6,905.

 

• Average of whole class = 6,905 ÷ 75 = 92.0666... ≈ 92.1 (rounded to one decimal place).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Weighted average = (n1 × a1 + n2 × a2) ÷ (n1 + n2); plug in directly without separately writing every intermediate total if working under time pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options in the source show only the decimal part with a stray 'X)' prefix (e.g. 'C).1'), a formatting glitch in the original document — the full computed value is 92.1, matching option C exactly in its decimal part.

question: The amount on a sum of ₹4,400 at the rate of 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹6,336.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹4,400; rate = 20% per annum, compounded annually; time = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ = 4,400 × (1 + 20/100)² = 4,400 × (1.2)².

 

• (1.2)² = 1.44.

 

• Amount = 4,400 × 1.44 = ₹6,336.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 2 years at rate R%, effective growth factor = (1+R/100)² = 1 + 2R/100 + (R/100)²; for R=20%, this is 1 + 0.40 + 0.04 = 1.44 — apply directly to the principal.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse this with simple interest, which for the same numbers would give only 4,400 × 1.40 = ₹6,160 — the extra ₹176 here is interest-on-interest, the hallmark of compounding.

question: The number of prime numbers lying between 309 and 320 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Range: integers strictly between 309 and 320, i.e. 310 to 319.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check each number: 310 (even), 311 (prime), 312 (even), 313 (prime), 314 (even), 315 (divisible by 5), 316 (even), 317 (prime), 318 (even), 319 = 11 × 29 (not prime).

 

• Primes found: 311, 313, 317 — that is 3 primes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Quickly eliminate all even numbers and multiples of 5 first, then test only the remaining few odd candidates for divisibility by small primes (3, 7, 11, 13, 17) up to √320 ≈ 17.9.

 

NOTE

 

• A number n is prime if it has no divisor other than 1 and itself; to test it, it is enough to check divisibility by primes up to √n.

question: Two trains, 170 metres and 220 metres in length, are running in opposite directions. The first runs at the rate of 45 km/hr and the second at the rate of 63 km/hr. How long will they take to cross each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 13 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train lengths: 170 m and 220 m; speeds: 45 km/hr and 63 km/hr, moving in opposite directions.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total distance to cover = sum of lengths = 170 + 220 = 390 m.

 

• Relative speed (opposite directions) = 45 + 63 = 108 km/hr = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s.

 

• Time = distance ÷ speed = 390 ÷ 30 = 13 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert km/hr to m/s using the multiplier 5/18 (and m/s to km/hr using 18/5) — memorising this conversion saves time in every trains question.

 

NOTE

 

• Two trains crossing each other (opposite directions) always cover a distance equal to the sum of their lengths, at a relative speed equal to the sum of their speeds.

question: Which of the following is NOT a prime number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 51.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers to test: 51, 31, 79, 67.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 51 = 3 × 17, so it has factors other than 1 and itself — not prime.

 

• 31: not divisible by 2, 3, or 5 (√31 ≈ 5.6, so only these need checking) — prime.

 

• 79: not divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7 (√79 ≈ 8.9) — prime.

 

• 67: not divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7 (√67 ≈ 8.2) — prime.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For any 2-digit number, quickly check divisibility by 3 (digit sum) and by 7 and 11 (since 2 and 5 are ruled out by the last digit) — 5+1=6 is divisible by 3, immediately flagging 51 as composite.

 

NOTE

 

• The digit-sum test for divisibility by 3 (sum of digits divisible by 3 ⇒ number divisible by 3) is the fastest way to spot composite numbers like 51 in prime-checking questions.

question: Maya buys a mobile phone for her child. The phone is marked at ₹21,000 and is offered with two successive discounts of 5% and Z%, respectively. After receiving both discounts, she pays ₹11,172. Find the value of Z.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 44.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price = ₹21,000; successive discounts of 5% and Z%; final price paid = ₹11,172.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After the first discount of 5%: 21,000 × 0.95 = ₹19,950.

 

• After the second discount of Z%: 19,950 × (1 − Z/100) = 11,172.

 

• (1 − Z/100) = 11,172 ÷ 19,950 = 0.56.

 

• Z/100 = 1 − 0.56 = 0.44 ⇒ Z = 44.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For successive discounts a% and b%, net multiplying factor = (1−a/100)(1−b/100); here (0.95)(1−Z/100) = 11172/21000 = 0.532, so (1−Z/100) = 0.532/0.95 = 0.56 ⇒ Z = 44.

 

NOTE

 

• Successive discounts are never simply added (5% + Z% ≠ total discount) — each discount applies to the price remaining after the previous discount, so they must be multiplied as factors.

question:
The curved surface area and the volume of a cylindrical pipe is 565.2 m² and 1,695.6 m³, respectively. Find the total surface area of the pipe.

(Use π = 3.14)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 791.28 m².

 

GIVEN

 

• Curved surface area (CSA) = 565.2 m²; Volume = 1,695.6 m³; π = 3.14.

 

SOLUTION

 

• CSA = 2πrh = 565.2 ⇒ rh = 565.2 ÷ (2 × 3.14) = 565.2 ÷ 6.28 = 90.

 

• Volume = πr²h = 1,695.6 ⇒ r²h = 1,695.6 ÷ 3.14 = 540.

 

• Dividing: r²h ÷ rh = r = 540 ÷ 90 = 6 m. Then h = 90 ÷ r = 90 ÷ 6 = 15 m.

 

• Total surface area = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × 3.14 × 6 × (15 + 6) = 37.68 × 21 = 791.28 m².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Get r directly as (volume ÷ CSA) × 2, since r²h/rh = r and volume/CSA = (πr²h)/(2πrh) = r/2, so r = 2 × (volume/CSA) = 2 × (1695.6/565.2) = 2 × 3 = 6, then find h and finish as above.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options in the source keep only the decimal part after a stray 'X)' prefix (e.g. 'B).28 m2') — a formatting glitch in the original document. The full computed value, 791.28 m², matches option B exactly in its decimal part.

question: R's age is twice the age of S and three times the age of T. S is 5 years older than T. What is the difference in ages (in years) between R and T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• R = 2S = 3T; S = T + 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• From R = 3T and R = 2S: 3T = 2S = 2(T+5) = 2T + 10.

 

• 3T − 2T = 10 ⇒ T = 10.

 

• S = T + 5 = 15; R = 3T = 30.

 

• Difference between R and T = 30 − 10 = 20.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express everything in terms of T immediately (R = 3T, S = T+5, and R = 2S gives 3T = 2T+10), solving in a single equation rather than juggling three separate variables.

 

NOTE

 

• Always pick the variable that appears in the most relations (here T) as the base variable to minimise the number of substitutions needed.

question: The monthly incomes of two friends, David and Ajay, are in the ratio 5 : 8, and each of them saves ₹72,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 4, find the monthly income of David (in ₹).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹90,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Income ratio David : Ajay = 5 : 8; each saves ₹72,000/month; expenditure ratio David : Ajay = 1 : 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let incomes = 5k and 8k. Since savings = income − expenditure, expenditures = (5k − 72,000) and (8k − 72,000).

 

• Given ratio of expenditures = 1 : 4: 4(5k − 72,000) = 1(8k − 72,000).

 

• 20k − 2,88,000 = 8k − 72,000 ⇒ 12k = 2,16,000 ⇒ k = 18,000.

 

• David's income = 5k = 5 × 18,000 = ₹90,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set incomes as 5k, 8k directly from the given ratio, express both expenditures in terms of k using the common savings figure, and cross-multiply the expenditure ratio — this collapses the whole problem to one linear equation in k.

 

NOTE

 

• Savings = Income − Expenditure is the key linking relation whenever a question mixes ratios of income, expenditure and a common savings amount.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 11 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 22 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 11.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills the tank in 11 minutes. Emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 22 minutes. Both opened together on an empty tank; find time to fill half the tank.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Rate of filling pipe = 1/11 (tank per minute). Rate of emptying pipe = −1/22 (tank per minute).

 

• Combined rate (both open) = 1/11 − 1/22 = 2/22 − 1/22 = 1/22 of the tank per minute.

 

• Time to fill half (1/2) the tank = (1/2) ÷ (1/22) = (1/2) × 22 = 11 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined rate here works out to exactly half the filling pipe's own rate (1/22 vs 1/11), so filling half the tank together takes exactly as long as filling the whole tank with the filling pipe alone — both equal 11 minutes.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract the emptying pipe's rate (treat it as negative work) from the filling pipe's rate to get the net combined rate when pipes work against each other.

question: 3 cups and 4 glasses cost ₹270. If 2 more glasses are purchased, then the total amount becomes ₹330. Find the cost of a cup.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ₹50.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 cups + 4 glasses = ₹270. Adding 2 more glasses (so 3 cups + 6 glasses) = ₹330.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Extra cost for 2 extra glasses = 330 − 270 = ₹60, so cost of 1 glass = 60 ÷ 2 = ₹30.

 

• Substitute back: 3 cups + 4(30) = 270 ⇒ 3 cups + 120 = 270 ⇒ 3 cups = 150.

 

• Cost of 1 cup = 150 ÷ 3 = ₹50.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since only the number of glasses changed between the two totals, the price difference (₹60) directly gives the price of 2 glasses — isolate that variable first before solving for the cup.

 

NOTE

 

• In simultaneous linear equations, always look for a pair of conditions that differ in only one variable — it lets you solve for that variable without elimination or substitution algebra.

question: A trader buys an article and sells it at a profit of 25%. The buyer again sells it at a loss of 10%. If the final selling price is ₹9,900, then what was the cost price (in ₹) of the article for the first trader?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹8,800.

 

GIVEN

 

• First trader sells at 25% profit; the buyer (second trader) sells that at a 10% loss; final selling price = ₹9,900.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the first trader's cost price = CP1. His selling price (= second trader's cost price, CP2) = CP1 × 1.25.

 

• The second trader sells at a 10% loss: CP2 × 0.90 = 9,900 ⇒ CP2 = 9,900 ÷ 0.90 = ₹11,000.

 

• CP1 = CP2 ÷ 1.25 = 11,000 ÷ 1.25 = ₹8,800.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Chain the multipliers and work backwards from the final price: CP1 = Final SP ÷ (1.25 × 0.90) = 9,900 ÷ 1.125 = ₹8,800, in a single step.

 

NOTE

 

• In a chain of successive profit/loss transactions, always multiply (not add) the successive factors, and work backward from the last known value to the first.

question: Simplify: 72 − [49 − (81 ÷ 9 − (14 − 24 ÷ 4) ÷ 8)]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 31.

 

GIVEN

 

• 72 − [49 − (81 ÷ 9 − (14 − 24 ÷ 4) ÷ 8)].

 

SOLUTION (innermost bracket outward)

 

• Innermost: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, so (14 − 6) = 8.

 

• Next: 8 ÷ 8 = 1.

 

• Next: 81 ÷ 9 = 9, so (9 − 1) = 8.

 

• Next: 49 − 8 = 41.

 

• Final: 72 − 41 = 31.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Work strictly from the innermost bracket outward, resolving one layer at a time — writing intermediate results as you go avoids sign errors in nested-bracket questions like this.

 

NOTE

 

• Follow VBODMAS strictly: solve the innermost parentheses first, then divisions, before moving to the outer brackets.

question: The cost price of a box of notebooks is ₹7,400. The shopkeeper gave 28% discount on the cost price. What will be the selling price (in ₹)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹5,328.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost price = ₹7,400; discount = 28% on the cost price.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Discount amount = 28% of 7,400 = 0.28 × 7,400 = ₹2,072.

 

• Selling price = 7,400 − 2,072 = ₹5,328.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Selling price = CP × (1 − discount%) = 7,400 × 0.72 = ₹5,328, computed directly in one multiplication.

 

NOTE

 

• Note that here the discount is applied on the cost price, not a marked/listed price — read the question carefully, as this differs from the usual discount-on-marked-price setup.

question: Given that C is the third proportional of 59 and B. If B is the sum of the first three even natural numbers, then find the value of C. (Round off the answer to two decimal places.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 2.44.

 

GIVEN

 

• B = sum of the first three even natural numbers; C is the third proportional of 59 and B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• First three even natural numbers: 2, 4, 6. So B = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12.

 

• 'C is the third proportional of 59 and B' means 59 : B :: B : C, i.e. C = B²/59.

 

• C = 12² ÷ 59 = 144 ÷ 59 = 2.4407... ≈ 2.44 (rounded to two decimal places).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'third proportional of a and b', always use the formula c = b²/a directly — no need to set up the proportion from scratch each time.

 

NOTE

 

• The printed options in the source retain only the decimal part after a stray 'X)' prefix (e.g. 'C).44'), a formatting glitch in the original document — the computed value 2.44 matches option C's decimal part exactly.

question: If the expenditure of Company A in 2023 was ₹660 crore and the profit percentage was 35%, then what was its income in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ₹891 crore.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expenditure = ₹660 crore; profit = 35% (on expenditure).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit amount = 35% of 660 = 0.35 × 660 = ₹231 crore.

 

• Income = Expenditure + Profit = 660 + 231 = ₹891 crore.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Income = Expenditure × (1 + profit%) = 660 × 1.35 = ₹891 crore, in a single multiplication.

 

NOTE

 

• Here, profit% is calculated on the expenditure (cost), which is the standard convention unless a question explicitly states the profit is a percentage of income/revenue.

question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 15% and its height is increased by 149%, then what is the percentage increase (rounded to the nearest integer) in its volume?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 80%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Radius decreased by 15% (new radius = 0.85r); height increased by 149% (new height = 2.49h).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of cylinder V = πr²h, so new volume V' = π(0.85r)²(2.49h) = π r²h × (0.85)² × 2.49.

 

• (0.85)² = 0.7225.

 

• 0.7225 × 2.49 = 1.799025.

 

• So V'/V = 1.799025, meaning volume increases by (1.799025 − 1) × 100% = 79.9025% ≈ 80% (rounded to the nearest integer).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Multiply the scale factors of each dimension raised to their respective powers in the volume formula: (radius factor)² × (height factor) = (0.85)² × 2.49 ≈ 1.80, i.e. about 80% increase — no need to introduce actual numeric values for r and h.

 

NOTE

 

• Volume of a cylinder depends on r² (not just r), so a 15% decrease in radius must be squared when computing its effect on volume — a common place students forget to square the factor.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single digit numbers only. Counting to be done from left to right only.

 

(Left) 2 6 9 1 2 5 7 2 5 2 2 4 7 9 3 2 5 4 1 4 9 9 1 8 9 (Right)

 

How many such even digits is/are there each of which is immediately preceded by an even digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 2 6 9 1 2 5 7 2 5 2 2 4 7 9 3 2 5 4 1 4 9 9 1 8 9

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number the terms 1 to 25 and scan for an even digit whose immediate left neighbour AND immediate right neighbour are both even.

 

• Term-by-term, the only place this pattern occurs is at position 11 (value 2): the term before it (position 10) is 2 (even), and the term after it (position 12) is 4 (even). So (2, 2, 4) qualifies.

 

• Checking every other even digit in the series (positions 1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24) shows at least one neighbour is odd in each case, so none of them qualify.

 

• Only one even digit satisfies the condition (even–even–even).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every even digit first, then check only those positions for even neighbours on both sides — this is much faster than scanning the whole series digit by digit.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check both the immediate left AND immediate right neighbour before confirming a match — missing one side is the most common mistake in this question type.

question: Mr. Akai starts from Point A and drives 15 km towards the north. He then takes a right turn, drives 18 km, turns right and drives 23 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 26 km. He takes a final right turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 8 km to the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A, facing north; travel: 15 km north → right → 18 km → right → 23 km → right → 26 km → right → 8 km, stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Plot on a coordinate grid, taking A = (0, 0), north = +y, east = +x. Facing north, each 'right' turn changes the facing direction: north → east → south → west → north.

 

• 15 km north: (0, 15). Turn right (now facing east), 18 km: (18, 15).

 

• Turn right (now facing south), 23 km: (18, 15−23) = (18, −8).

 

• Turn right (now facing west), 26 km: (18−26, −8) = (−8, −8).

 

• Turn right (now facing north), 8 km: (−8, −8+8) = P = (−8, 0).

 

• Distance from P to A = |0 − (−8)| = 8 km, and since A(x=0) is to the right of P(x=−8) on the map, the direction from P to A is east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net east-west and north-south displacement instead of drawing the whole path: net E-W = −18+26 = wait, track x: +18 (east) −26 (west) = −8; net y: +15−23+8 = 0. So P is 8 km west of A along the x-axis, meaning A is 8 km east of P.

 

NOTE

 

• Set up a simple x-y coordinate system with the starting point at the origin — it avoids errors that come from trying to visualise multiple turns without a diagram.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster pair DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. QN-SP.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: QN-SP, UR-WS, WT-YU, SP-UQ.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to positions (A=1...Z=26) and find the shift from the first cluster to the second, letter by letter.

 

• UR-WS: U(21)→W(23) is +2; R(18)→S(19) is +1. Pattern: (+2, +1).

 

• WT-YU: W(23)→Y(25) is +2; T(20)→U(21) is +1. Pattern: (+2, +1).

 

• SP-UQ: S(19)→U(21) is +2; P(16)→Q(17) is +1. Pattern: (+2, +1).

 

• QN-SP: Q(17)→S(19) is +2; N(14)→P(16) is +2. Pattern: (+2, +2) — this breaks the (+2, +1) pattern followed by the other three.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert only the first letter of each cluster and the second letter of each cluster into two separate short number sequences, and look for the one pair that breaks the otherwise-common step pattern in either sequence.

 

NOTE

 

• When comparing letter-cluster pairs, always check BOTH letters' shifts separately — a pair can match on one letter's pattern and still be the odd one out because of the other letter.

question:
If + means -, - means x , x means ÷ , ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

 

21 - 4 ÷ 371 + 111 x 3 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 418.

 

GIVEN

 

• Symbol swap: '+' means '−', '−' means '×', '÷' means '+', '×' means '÷'. Evaluate: 21 − 4 ÷ 371 + 111 × 3.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its real meaning: '−' → '×', '÷' → '+', '+' → '−', '×' → '÷'.

 

• The expression becomes: 21 × 4 + 371 − 111 ÷ 3.

 

• Apply BODMAS on the converted expression: 21 × 4 = 84; 111 ÷ 3 = 37.

 

• 84 + 371 − 37 = 455 − 37 = 418.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the entire expression with the correct symbols FIRST, before doing any arithmetic — trying to apply the swapped meanings on the fly while calculating is the most common source of errors here.

 

NOTE

 

• After substituting the true symbol meanings, apply the normal order of operations (BODMAS) to the rewritten expression — the swap only changes what each symbol means, not the order in which operations are performed.

question: CEID is related to JLPK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, EGKF is related to LNRM. To which of the given options is GIMH related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. NPTO.

 

GIVEN

 

• CEID → JLPK; EGKF → LNRM; find GIMH → ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert letters to positions (A=1...Z=26) and check the shift, letter by letter: C(3)→J(10): +7; E(5)→L(12): +7; I(9)→P(16): +7; D(4)→K(11): +7.

 

• Verify with the second pair: E(5)→L(12): +7; G(7)→N(14): +7; K(11)→R(18): +7; F(6)→M(13): +7. Confirmed: each letter shifts forward by 7 positions.

 

• Apply the same +7 shift to G, I, M, H: G(7)→N(14); I(9)→P(16); M(13)→T(20); H(8)→O(15).
